blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Every October, the country marks the Special Month for the Conservation and Protection of the Tamaraw in Mindoro, highlighting efforts to protect one of the Philippines’ most iconic — and most threatened — animals. The observance was established in 2002 through Proclamation No. 273, signed by then-President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo, to increase public awareness of the tamaraw’s importance as part of the country’s natural heritage and biological resources. The declaration came after the country saw decades of decline in the tamaraw population. The world’s rarest buffalo, the species is found only on the island of Mindoro, southwest of Luzon. […]...
